body.statement: For the signed-depth alternatives, there exists \(B_0<\infty\), independent of \(Q\) and \(T\), such that \(\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{Q,+1}^{\mathrm{obs},T}\,\|\,\mathbb P_{Q,-1}^{\mathrm{obs},T})\le B_0T\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\). More precisely, for every observed history, \(E_v[Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{\mathrm{obs}}]=vc_0\varepsilon_Ca_t^{(Q)}q_t^v\) and \(q_t^v\le K_0\alpha^Q\) for a finite \(K_0\) depending only on \(t_0\), so the bound includes all stationary initial windows \(t\le Q\) without revealing reset times.
body.justification: This is the early kill test: the extra hidden-survival factor in observed KL is exactly what preserves the Hu--Wager exponent under fixed latent occupancy.
body.gap: HuWager2023, Lemma 3.3, proves the corresponding divergence bound for its unrestricted hard chain; no published argument located in the scan controls the full observed filter while every joint-state stationary ratio is uniformly bounded.
body.consumer: The lemma decides whether bounded latent occupancy alone can justify shorter histories in the mobile-health use case.
